The invention concerns a process for manufacturing and deburring gear teeth on workpieces (6). The system includes two workpiece spindles (3, 3′), a hobbing tool (12), and a deburring unit (10). The workpieces (6) are automatically secured in the workpiece spindles (3, 3′), cut with teeth by the hobbing tool (12), and subsequently deburred.

The method comprises the following sequence:

a. A first workpiece spindle (3) takes up an unprocessed workpiece (6) at a first loading position (19) and conveys it to the hobbing tool (12).

b. A milling cut is performed.

c. The workpiece (6) is deposited again at the first loading position (19), and another untreated workpiece (6) is picked up.

d. The workpiece (6) that has undergone the milling cut is transferred to a second loading position (19′).

e. At the second loading position (19′), the second workpiece spindle (3′) receives the workpiece (6) and moves it to the deburring tool (10).

f. The workpiece (6) is deburred.

An intermediate storage location (14) for at least one workpiece (6) is arranged between the first loading position (19) and the second loading position (19′). The workpiece (6) is shifted from this intermediate storage (14) into the second loading position (19′). Steps e and f are performed during the same period of time in which step b is also being carried out.

The invention relates to a method for producing and deburring toothings on workpieces, in particular gear workpieces. The method uses a machining system comprising two workpiece spindles, a hobbing tool, and a deburring device. By coordinating the movements of the two workpiece spindles and the transfer of the workpieces between different loading positions, the method allows hobbing and deburring operations to be carried out at least partially in parallel, thereby improving productivity.

In a first step, an unmachined workpiece is received by a first workpiece spindle in a first loading position. The first workpiece spindle then transports the unmachined workpiece to the hobbing tool. At the hobbing tool, the workpiece is machined by a milling operation, in particular by a mill cut, in order to produce the desired toothing on the workpiece.

After completion of the hobbing operation, the first workpiece spindle transports the now-machined workpiece back to the first loading position. At this stage, the machined workpiece can be removed from the first spindle, while another unmachined workpiece is received by the first spindle for a subsequent hobbing operation. In this way, the first spindle continues to supply the hobbing tool with unmachined workpieces for machining.

The workpiece that has already been machined by the hobbing tool is then transferred from the first loading position to an intermediate storage area. From this intermediate storage area, the machined workpiece is moved to a second loading position. In the second loading position, the machined workpiece is received by a second workpiece spindle. The second workpiece spindle then transports the machined workpiece to the deburring device.

At the deburring device, burrs or machining residues produced during the hobbing process are removed from the machined toothing. The deburring operation is carried out while another unmachined workpiece, previously received by the first workpiece spindle, is being machined by the hobbing tool. As a result, the hobbing of one workpiece and the deburring of another workpiece take place simultaneously.

This parallel processing reduces idle times of the hobbing tool and the deburring device and enables a more efficient production sequence. The use of two workpiece spindles, together with the intermediate storage area and separate loading positions, allows the machining and deburring steps to be coordinated in a continuous workflow. Consequently, the method increases throughput in the production of toothed workpieces while ensuring that each workpiece is both hobbed and deburred before leaving the machining system.
outputs.L4:
A method is provided for producing and deburring gear toothings on workpieces in an efficient machining arrangement. The method uses at least two workpiece spindles, a hobbing tool for cutting the gear teeth, a deburring device for removing burrs produced during the cutting operation, and an intermediate storage system for transferring workpieces between different loading and machining positions.

In operation, a first workpiece is clamped on a first workpiece spindle and machined by the hobbing tool to produce the desired gear toothing. After the hobbing operation, the workpiece may contain burrs or sharp edges, particularly at the tooth ends or along the machined profile. These burrs are removed by the deburring device in a separate deburring operation. At the same time, a second workpiece is clamped on a second workpiece spindle and is machined by the hobbing tool. In this way, the deburring of one workpiece and the hobbing of another workpiece take place at least partly simultaneously.

The intermediate storage system supports this coordinated sequence by receiving workpieces from one loading position and transferring them to another position for further machining or unloading. It may temporarily hold a machined or partially machined workpiece while another workpiece is being processed, allowing the spindles, hobbing tool, and deburring device to be used more continuously. The storage system therefore acts as a buffer between the hobbing and deburring stages and helps synchronize the workpiece flow through the machine.

By arranging the process so that deburring is not performed only after all hobbing operations have stopped, the idle time of the machining equipment is significantly reduced. While one spindle is occupied with a deburring step, the other spindle can already be used for producing a new gear toothing. This parallel processing increases the utilization of the machine components, shortens the overall production cycle, and improves manufacturing efficiency. The method is particularly suitable for the series production of toothed workpieces, such as gears, pinions, and similar components requiring both accurate tooth cutting and reliable burr removal.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in everyday communication. It is called a definite article, and it helps us point to something specific. For example, when we say “the book,” we are not talking about any book, but a particular one that the listener can identify.

Although “the” may seem simple, it gives clarity and structure to sentences. It helps readers and listeners understand whether we are discussing something general or something already known. Without words like “the,” language would feel less precise and more difficult to follow.

In writing, “the” often appears so naturally that we barely notice it. However, its presence can change the meaning of a sentence. “A house” could be any house, but “the house” refers to a specific house. This small difference shows how powerful even the simplest words can be.

In conclusion, “the” is more than just a common word. It is a key part of English grammar, helping people communicate clearly, accurately, and effectively.

## Abstract

An automated method and apparatus for machining workpieces, in particular toothed workpieces, are disclosed. A workpiece is supplied to a first loading station and transferred to a first work spindle, where the workpiece is machined by a milling tool, preferably by hobbing. After the milling operation, the workpiece is transferred from the first work spindle to an intermediate store. The intermediate store conveys the workpiece to a second loading station associated with a second work spindle. The workpiece is then received by the second work spindle and subjected to a deburring operation by a deburring tool. The use of the intermediate store decouples the milling operation from the deburring operation and permits automated transfer of workpieces between the respective loading stations. The method enables continuous or substantially continuous machining of successive workpieces with improved utilization of the milling and deburring spindles.

## Exemplary Independent Method Claim

1. A method for automated machining of workpieces, comprising:  
   supplying a workpiece to a first loading station;  
   transferring the workpiece from the first loading station to a first work spindle;  
   rotating the workpiece on the first work spindle and machining the workpiece with a milling tool to produce a milled workpiece;  
   transferring the milled workpiece from the first work spindle to an intermediate store;  
   conveying the milled workpiece by the intermediate store to a second loading station;  
   transferring the milled workpiece from the second loading station to a second work spindle; and  
   rotating the milled workpiece on the second work spindle and deburring the milled workpiece with a deburring tool.

## Exemplary Dependent Claims

2. The method of claim 1, wherein the machining with the milling tool comprises hobbing a tooth profile on the workpiece.

3. The method of claim 1, wherein the first work spindle and the second work spindle operate independently of one another.

4. The method of claim 1, wherein the intermediate store temporarily buffers a plurality of workpieces between the first loading station and the second loading station.

5. The method of claim 1, wherein the intermediate store transfers workpieces in a timed sequence coordinated with operating cycles of the first work spindle and the second work spindle.

6. The method of claim 1, wherein a further workpiece is machined on the first work spindle while the milled workpiece is deburred on the second work spindle.

7. The method of claim 1, wherein the workpiece is transferred between at least one of the loading stations and the respective work spindle by a handling device.

8. The method of claim 1, wherein the intermediate store comprises a rotary store, linear store, conveyor, pallet store, or indexed transfer device.

9. The method of claim 1, wherein the deburring operation comprises removing burrs from tooth edges formed during hobbing.

10. The method of claim 1, wherein the workpiece remains oriented in a predetermined angular position during transfer from the first work spindle to the second work spindle.

## Exemplary Independent Apparatus Claim

11. An apparatus for automated machining of workpieces, comprising:  
   a first loading station;  
   a first work spindle configured to receive a workpiece from the first loading station and to rotate the workpiece during machining by a milling tool;  
   a second loading station;  
   a second work spindle configured to receive a machined workpiece from the second loading station and to rotate the machined workpiece during deburring by a deburring tool; and  
   an intermediate store arranged between the first loading station and the second loading station and configured to transfer machined workpieces from the first work spindle to the second loading station.

## Additional Dependent Apparatus Claims

12. The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the milling tool is a hob configured to generate a toothed profile on the workpiece.

13. The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the intermediate store is configured to buffer a plurality of workpieces.

14. The apparatus of claim 11, further comprising a control unit configured to coordinate operation of the first work spindle, the second work spindle, and the intermediate store.

15. The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the first work spindle and the second work spindle are arranged in separate machining stations.

16. The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the intermediate store comprises a plurality of receiving positions for holding respective workpieces.

17. The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the second work spindle is configured to perform chamfering, brushing, scraping, cutting, or rolling deburring.

18. The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the intermediate store is configured to transfer a workpiece from an output position associated with the first work spindle to an input position associated with the second work spindle without manual intervention.

counterfactuals.output:
## Invention Description

### Method for Producing and Deburring Toothings on Workpieces

The invention relates to a method for producing and deburring toothings on workpieces, in particular gear workpieces, wherein a toothing is produced by a milling tool on a workpiece held on a first workpiece spindle, and wherein a previously produced toothing on another workpiece is deburred on a second workpiece spindle during the same machining cycle.

### Reference Numerals

1 — machine tool  
2 — machine frame  
3 — first workpiece spindle  
4 — second workpiece spindle  
5 — first workpiece  
6 — second workpiece  
7 — milling tool  
8 — deburring tool  
9 — tool spindle  
10 — deburring spindle or deburring unit  
11 — toothing  
12 — burr  
13 — control unit  
14 — machining position  
15 — deburring position  
16 — loading and unloading device  
17 — rotation axis of first workpiece spindle  
18 — rotation axis of second workpiece spindle  
19 — rotation axis of milling tool  
20 — rotation axis of deburring tool  

---

### General Description

A method is provided for producing and deburring toothings 11 on workpieces 5, 6 in a machine tool 1. The machine tool 1 comprises at least a first workpiece spindle 3 and a second workpiece spindle 4. The first workpiece spindle 3 is configured to hold and rotate a first workpiece 5 about a first rotation axis 17. The second workpiece spindle 4 is configured to hold and rotate a second workpiece 6 about a second rotation axis 18.

A milling tool 7, preferably a hob, profile milling cutter, generating milling cutter, or skiving-type milling tool, is arranged on a tool spindle 9 and is configured to produce a toothing 11 on the first workpiece 5 by a mill cut. A deburring tool 8 is arranged on a deburring spindle or deburring unit 10 and is configured to remove burrs 12 from a previously produced toothing 11 of the second workpiece 6.

The method is characterized in that the deburring of the toothing 11 of the second workpiece 6 on the second workpiece spindle 4 is carried out during the same time interval in which the milling tool 7 performs the mill cut for producing the toothing 11 on the first workpiece 5 on the first workpiece spindle 3. As a result, the deburring operation does not require a separate additional cycle time after completion of the mill cut on the first workpiece 5. Instead, the deburring operation is performed in parallel with the cutting operation on another workpiece.

---

### Enumerated Method Steps

A method for producing and deburring toothings 11 on workpieces 5, 6 comprises the following steps:

**Step S1: Providing the machine tool**  
Providing a machine tool 1 having a machine frame 2, a first workpiece spindle 3, a second workpiece spindle 4, a milling tool 7, a deburring tool 8, and a control unit 13.

**Step S2: Clamping a first workpiece**  
Clamping a first workpiece 5 on the first workpiece spindle 3, wherein the first workpiece 5 is positioned in a machining position 14 for producing a toothing 11.

**Step S3: Clamping a second workpiece**  
Clamping a second workpiece 6 on the second workpiece spindle 4, wherein the second workpiece 6 already has a toothing 11 produced in a preceding machining operation and is positioned in a deburring position 15.

**Step S4: Producing a toothing on the first workpiece**  
Rotating the first workpiece 5 about the first rotation axis 17 and driving the milling tool 7 about the tool rotation axis 19, and producing the toothing 11 on the first workpiece 5 by carrying out a mill cut with the milling tool 7.

**Step S5: Deburring the second workpiece during the mill cut**  
During the same time interval in which the mill cut according to step S4 is performed on the first workpiece 5, rotating the second workpiece 6 about the second rotation axis 18 and engaging the deburring tool 8 with the toothing 11 of the second workpiece 6 in order to remove burrs 12 from the second workpiece 6.

**Step S6: Coordinated control of milling and deburring**  
Controlling, by means of the control unit 13, the movements and rotational speeds of the first workpiece spindle 3, the second workpiece spindle 4, the milling tool 7, and the deburring tool 8 such that the milling operation on the first workpiece 5 and the deburring operation on the second workpiece 6 are performed at least partially simultaneously, preferably completely simultaneously over a common machining interval.

**Step S7: Completion of the parallel operations**  
Completing the mill cut on the first workpiece 5 and completing the deburring operation on the second workpiece 6 within the same machining cycle, such that the second workpiece 6 is deburred before or at the time the toothing 11 of the first workpiece 5 has been fully produced.

**Step S8: Unloading and indexing of workpieces**  
Removing the deburred second workpiece 6 from the second workpiece spindle 4 by means of a loading and unloading device 16 and transferring the first workpiece 5, after production of its toothing 11, to a subsequent deburring operation on the second workpiece spindle 4 or another deburring position 15.

**Step S9: Repetition in a production sequence**  
Repeating steps S2 to S8 in a continuous production sequence, wherein a toothing 11 is produced on one workpiece while a toothing 11 previously produced on another workpiece is deburred in parallel.

---

### Detailed Description of the Method

In operation, a first workpiece 5 is received by the first workpiece spindle 3. The milling tool 7 is brought into engagement with the first workpiece 5 in order to generate the toothing 11. During this mill cut, material is removed from the first workpiece 5, whereby burrs 12 may be formed at axial or radial end regions of the toothing 11.

At the same time, a second workpiece 6, on which a toothing 11 has already been produced in a preceding cycle, is held by the second workpiece spindle 4. The deburring tool 8 is brought into engagement with the second workpiece 6 in order to remove burrs 12 from the toothing 11. The deburring tool 8 may be formed as a deburring cutter, chamfering tool, brush, scraping tool, rolling deburring tool, or another suitable tool for removing burrs or producing chamfers on the tooth edges.

The essential feature of the method is that the deburring operation on the second workpiece 6 is not carried out after the mill cut on the first workpiece 5 has been completed, but rather during the same time interval as the mill cut on the first workpiece 5. Thus, while the milling tool 7 machines the first workpiece 5, the deburring tool 8 simultaneously deburrs the second workpiece 6. In this way, the deburring time is at least partially, and preferably completely, masked by the time required for producing the toothing 11 on the first workpiece 5.

The control unit 13 coordinates the machining operations in such a manner that no collision occurs between the tools 7, 8, the workpieces 5, 6, or other machine components. The first workpiece spindle 3 and the second workpiece spindle 4 may be arranged in parallel, opposite, or otherwise spatially separated positions on the machine frame 2. The machining position 14 and the deburring position 15 may be simultaneously occupied.

After completion of the milling operation on the first workpiece 5, the first workpiece 5 may be transferred to the second workpiece spindle 4 for deburring during a subsequent cycle. At the same time, a new workpiece may be loaded onto the first workpiece spindle 3 for production of a toothing 11. The method therefore enables a continuous flow of workpieces through the machine tool 1, wherein each workpiece is first toothed and subsequently deburred, while the deburring operation of one workpiece is performed in parallel with the toothing operation of another workpiece.

---

### Advantageous Effects

The described method provides a significant reduction in total cycle time because the deburring operation is integrated into the machining cycle and is performed during the mill cut of another workpiece. Since the second workpiece 6 is deburred while the first workpiece 5 is being toothed, the deburring process does not substantially extend the overall production time.

The method further improves machine utilization because the deburring tool 8 and the second workpiece spindle 4 are operated while the milling tool 7 and the first workpiece spindle 3 are simultaneously active. The method is particularly advantageous in series production of toothed workpieces, such as gears, pinions, shafts with external toothings, internally toothed components, or other workpieces having gear-like profiles.

A further advantage is that the workpiece flow can be organized in a simple indexed sequence: a workpiece is toothed on the first workpiece spindle 3, then deburred on the second workpiece spindle 4 while a following workpiece is toothed on the first workpiece spindle 3, and finally unloaded after deburring. This results in reduced idle time and increased throughput.

---

### Exemplary Claim-Like Formulation

A method for producing and deburring toothings 11 on workpieces 5, 6, comprising:

1. clamping a first workpiece 5 on a first workpiece spindle 3;  
2. clamping a second workpiece 6, having a previously produced toothing 11, on a second workpiece spindle 4;  
3. producing a toothing 11 on the first workpiece 5 by performing a mill cut with a milling tool 7; and  
4. deburring the previously produced toothing 11 of the second workpiece 6 with a deburring tool 8;  

wherein the deburring of the second workpiece 6 on the second workpiece spindle 4 is carried out during the same time interval as the mill cut performed by the milling tool 7 on the first workpiece 5.
